Pricing

Start free. Upgrade when your client list grows.

Free

Start free
  • Up to 3 clients
  • Unlimited invoices
  • Automatic payment reminders
  • Owed-at-a-glance dashboard
  • Card and bank transfer payments

Pro

$12per month

For freelancers with a busy roster who want invoices that look like their own.

Start free, upgrade later
  • Everything in Free
  • Unlimited clients
  • Your logo and brand colors
  • Recurring invoices
  • Automatic late fees

FAQ

Questions, answered

Is the free plan really free?

Yes. No credit card, no trial clock. You can invoice up to 3 clients for as long as you like.

What counts as a client?

A client is any person or business you send invoices to. You can send as many invoices as you need to each one.

Will the reminders sound pushy?

Only if you want them to. You choose when each reminder goes out and can edit every message before turning it on. The default wording is polite and to the point.

What happens when I add a fourth client?

Ledgerly will ask you to move to Pro for $12 a month. Invoices and reminders for your existing clients keep working either way.

Can I cancel Pro at any time?

Yes. Cancel from your settings and you'll drop back to the free plan at the end of your billing month.

Your next invoice could chase itself.

Create your free account in under a minute. Free for up to 3 clients, no credit card needed.

content.text:
I've built the Ledgerly landing page. It's three files in the project folder: `index.html`, `styles.css` and `script.js`. It opens straight from disk with no build step or server. Only the fonts (Fraunces and Inter) load from Google Fonts. The logo, favicon, icons and product mockups are all inline SVG or CSS, so no images come from other sites.

I couldn't open it in a browser here, so I haven't checked it at 390px or 1440px. The layout is written to switch for narrow screens: one column on phones, two on wide screens, and the email field and button stack on very narrow phones.

**What's on the page, top to bottom:**
- **Header:** stays at the top while scrolling, with a "Start free" button. On phones the menu links and "Sign in" are hidden, leaving the logo and that button.
- **Hero:** the headline "Get paid without the awkward follow‑ups.", a one-line pitch, and an email sign-up form with "Free for up to 3 clients" and "No credit card needed" under it. Beside it is a mockup of the dashboard showing what you're owed: a total, a bar split into due soon, late and 30+ days, and a list of recent invoices. A small pop-up on the mockup switches between "Reminder sent" and "Payment received".
- **Features:** one block each for sending invoices, chasing late payments automatically and seeing what you're owed, each with a small drawing of that part of the product.
- **How it works:** three steps.
- **Pricing:** Free and Pro ($12 a month). Free is the highlighted plan, and Pro's button also says "Start free, upgrade later", so every route leads to a free sign-up.
- **FAQ:** five questions that expand when clicked.
- **Final sign-up section** on a dark background, then the footer.

**Before you use it for real:**
- **The sign-up forms aren't connected to anything.** They check the email address and show a "You're in" message, but nothing is sent or saved. You'll need to point them at your sign-up service.
- **"Sign in" is a placeholder.** It jumps to the hero sign-up form.
- **I made up some product details.** Unlimited invoices, card and bank transfer payments, the 3/7/14-day reminder schedule, and Pro's branding, recurring invoices and late fees are all my guesses. So are the FAQ answers about cancelling and adding a fourth client. Please check them against what Ledgerly actually does.
- **No testimonials or user numbers.** I left these out on purpose rather than invent them.
